Reading the duct pressure before the starts
The landing altitude and barometric setting
The anti-skid test (it is armed) and the landing autobrake selection
APU, Pneu Supplies & Packs, APU/ISOL Valve (As Required); Water System (Depressurized)
Any change: the panel is left as it is

blocks.title: KC-10
rows: Voice Recorder, Longitudinal Trim System, Takeoff Warning Horn, Passenger Address System (TEST)
Setting the IFF on the CDUs
Passing 10,000 ft, both ways; Approach; Parking
Seat Belt Sign; Cabin Signs (ON); Seat Belts Sw (OFF)
The tanker's seat belt switch is never moved by the crew
The landing altitude and the FMS barometric setting
FMS, radio, crypto, SATCOM, IFF Mode 4 and data cartridge items
Radar, lights, thrust computer, flap selector, seat belt switch, and the gear and flap calls

blocks.title: MD-10
rows: Air Conditioning; Hydraulic Control Panel; Anti-Skid; Transponder/TCAS
The APU air and ECON switches, the hydraulic pressure test, the anti-skid test and the TCAS test
FUEL Control Panel; Fuel Panel (AUTO or MAN CKD)
The fuel panel's [MANUAL] check, even with its SYSTEM in MANUAL
Initializing the IRS; the voice recorder test
With the fuel SYSTEM in MANUAL, the transfer pumps and fill valves
Nothing to do: the MD-10 has no autobrake selector

blocks.content: A few items depend on something that happens on its own schedule, and holding the whole checklist for it would be wrong. For these the crew member starts the item, then lets the walk go on while watching for it in the background; they answer the item when it comes. The watched row stays light green until then, and the run is complete only when every watched item is answered. If the walk reaches the end first, the strip shows the badge of the seat that is still watching.

rows: After Takeoff: Flaps & Slats (DC-10), Flap/Slats (KC-10), FLAPS/SLATS (MD-10)
The flap and slat surfaces up, as you retract them on schedule. The spoilers and the rest go on meanwhile. On the MD-10 the F/O then sets the FLAP T.O. selector to 0
The radar test pattern, which the tanker's transmitter paints only after a warm-up of about three minutes from power-on; watched for up to four minutes
Descending below 14,000 ft before GA is selected, if the checklist was started higher
Preliminary Cockpit Preparation: Engine/APU Fire Test, Battery Power Only
AC on the buses, after which the test is repeated with AC power, as the FCOM requires
The test pattern on each radar system after its transmitter delay (about three minutes from power-on, about 90 seconds after a system swap)

blocks.content: If a watched item fails, for example a radar test that never sweeps, the run does not drop it: at the end of the walk it waits on you, with the crew member's note, until you tick that item.

children.title: When the crew calls or asks

blocks.content: Some items need something only you can give: your hand on the gear or flaps, a cart from the ramp, or a decision. The crew member then says so in the bubble and keeps waiting for it. The run's strip shows the same note and names CAPT (P on the KC-10) as having the item. When the thing arrives, the crew member's own wait answers the item and the walk goes on; there is nothing to acknowledge. Your tick also answers it.

blocks.title: Calls for your controls
rows: The gear is up and locked. The call waits for 50 ft above the runway and a positive rate, however early the checklist was started, and is not made if the gear is already up
Every gear leg down and locked
“Flaps and slats for landing.” (MD-10: “Flaps for landing.”)
The flap handle in the landing range (35° or more) and the slats extended for landing
“Flaps and slats are not at the takeoff setting.”
The flap surfaces within 0.5° of the takeoff card's FLAP (with no card, the handle in the takeoff range) and the slats extended. Said only after 30 seconds of waiting silently
“Trim is not at the takeoff setting.” (MD-10: “Stabilizer trim is not at the takeoff setting.”)
The stabilizer within 0.3° of the card's STAB (with no card, inside the green band) and, on the DC-10 and KC-10, aileron and rudder trim at zero. Said only after 20 seconds

blocks.title: Requests for ground equipment
rows: “APU did not start. Call for ground power and ground air.”
A ground power cart is plugged in and its power reaches the buses; the S/O selects EXT PWR
“APU power did not come on line. Call for ground power and ground air.”
DC-10: S/O Pre-Flight, APU. KC-10: FE's initial inspection, Electrical Power; Scramble
“No APU. Call for ground power and ground air.”
FE's initial inspection: Electrical Power (APU/External); Scramble
“No air for the start. Call for ground air.”
The APU running or a ground air cart coupled
A ground power cart plugged in
“Ground equipment still at the aircraft. Have it removed.”
Before Taxi: Ground Equipment & Gear Pins
No chocks in, no ground air cart and no ground power cart connected

blocks.content: A ground request carries a **Ground Ops** button, in the bubble and in the run strip, which opens Ground Ops at its Ramp page where the carts and chocks are called and removed ([Ground power and air](ground-operations#ground-power-and-air), [Ramp items](ground-operations#ramp-items)). The message asks for ground power and ground air together because without the APU you need both, the cart for the buses and the air for the starts; the S/O's item itself waits only for the power cart.

blocks.title: Questions
rows: The item is passed with No. 2 not running: FedEx's delayed engine start. After Start and Before Taxi are then due on two engines, and BEFORE TAKEOFF's first item starts No. 2 during the taxi
The item is passed, and Before Taxi is due on two engines; the FE starts No. 2 during the taxi at BEFORE TAKEOFF's Number 2 Engine, as the -1 directs
The FE shuts No. 2 down and turns off tank 2's pumps, keeping the right aft pump on for a running APU

children.title: When an item cannot be done

blocks.content: Every crew item that acts ends in one of two ways: done, or stopped with a reason. A crew member never answers an item they could not do. When they cannot, because the aircraft is not in the state the item needs (an engine running where the parking brake is to be released, no chocks, a gear handle not down), because something did not happen in the time it should (an engine that does not turn, an APU that does not reach speed, flaps that do not retract), or because a test did not show what it should, they stop the run on that item.

items: The strip shows the reason in amber, prefixed by the seat: “F/O: No. 3 did not turn: check the start air”. The seat's badge stays on the strip, but the run is now waiting for **you**.
A stopped item normally raises no bubble: it is not a request. Glance at the strip when the crew goes quiet.

Put right whatever is wrong, or do the item yourself, then tick it. The run goes on from the next item. Ticking an item does not make a crew member try it again; if you want them to, Start the checklist again.

Where an item gave up part-way, it has put back what it would leave dangerous: an engine start that does not turn releases its start switch; a radar test that does not sweep parks the radar; a takeoff warning test that does not sound puts the thrust lever back to idle.

blocks.content: The full list of the crew's notes, with their causes, is in [Crew messages](#messages).

**Pause**, at the top of the running checklist, holds the run where it is. Nothing new is begun and nothing more is moved, including the items watched in the background, until you press **Resume**. **Stop**, in the run strip, ends the run: the item in progress and every watched item are abandoned, and the checklist is left with the ticks it has. Start it again to run it from the top.

Pausing, stopping or ticking an item while a crew member is holding a control leaves that control where their hand was: a test switch held in TEST, the pedestal stabilizer trim handle held at nose up or nose down during the after-landing trim, or on the MD-10 a thrust lever held forward during the takeoff warning test. Avoid interrupting those items; if you do, return the control yourself.

With every item answered, by you or the crew, and nothing left watched, the run is complete and the checklist shows COMPLETE. The strip disappears. Ticks are kept with the aircraft, on every screen and across a restart of the simulator, until you reset them or start that checklist again. On AUTO the crew then offers the next checklist when its point in the flight comes ([AUTO](#auto-offers)).

**DC-10.** The card's silent items (FedEx's ►) are run like the rest; the EFB does not draw the mark. PREFLIGHT runs on into the card: after CAPT AND F/O PRE-FLIGHT, Next opens BEFORE START. The card's STARTING ENGINES, BEFORE TAXI, PASSING 10,000 FT and LEAVING AIRCRAFT pages are additions (FedEx's start duties as items, the KC-10's Before Taxi, the climb and descent profiles' light changes, and a securing checklist) so that the crew has a checklist for everything it does. Five of the card's items are left out of the EFB's version: BEFORE START's Aircraft Log and Windows, BEFORE TAKEOFF's Briefing and Seat Belt & Harness, and APPROACH's Briefing.

**KC-10.** The book's last item on each checklist (“Before Start Checklist ... COMPLETED”) is the FE's, and the FE answers it. The local pattern and non-standard checklists can be started from the index and are worked by the crew ([Local pattern and non-standard checklists](#kc10-flow-nonstandard)).

**MD-10.** The F/O reads every checklist on the ground and, as pilot not flying, in the air. The EXTERIOR INSPECTION is entirely the captain's; the other PREFLIGHT checklists follow the FCOM's cockpit preparation flows.

sections.title: AUTO: the crew follows the flight
sections.summary: How the crew decides which checklist is due, the offer bubble, and the rules that move the offers along.

blocks.content: With either seat on AUTO the crew keeps track of where the flight has got to and offers each checklist when it falls due, in a bubble over every app: **Start Before Start Checklist?** **Start** begins the run and opens the checklist in Documents. **Not Now** declines it. Either answer passes that checklist, and the crew then looks for the next one. Nothing is offered while a run is under way: the next offer waits until the current checklist is complete or stopped.

The crew cannot hear a captain call for a checklist, so it judges the phase of flight from what any crew member could see: whether the aircraft is on the ground, its ground speed, how many engines are running (by N2, not by the gauges), whether AC power is on the buses, the parking brake, the height above the runway, the altitude and the vertical speed. Each checklist on the card is tied to one of the moments below.

rows: On the ground, stopped (under 1 kt), no engine running, the turnaround over
Interior Safety Check; Cockpit Inspection; Second Officer Pre-Flight; Capt and F/O Pre-Flight
FE's Exterior/Interior Initial Inspection; FE's Interior Inspection; FE's Exterior Inspection; Pilot's Interior Inspection
Cockpit Safety Inspection; Preliminary Cockpit Preparation; Captain's Cockpit Preparation; F/O Cockpit Preparation; Final Cockpit Preparation
As above, with AC power on a generator bus
Stopped, AC powered, fewer than three engines running
On the ground with three engines running (two, after a delayed No. 2)
On the ground, at least two engines running, faster than 5 kt
Airborne, more than 1,500 ft above the runway
Descending (more than 500 ft/min down, and at least 2,000 ft below the highest altitude of the flight) below 18,000 ft
Descending below 2,500 ft above the runway after a flight
On the ground after a flight, slower than 40 kt
On the ground after a flight, stopped, parking brake set

blocks.content: The descent moments need a real descent: a level-off at an intermediate altitude, or a climb after a dip, offers nothing. The cruise itself owes no checklist.

items: **The latest due.** The crew offers the latest checklist whose moment the flight has reached. Turn AUTO on while taxiing and the first offer is Before Takeoff, not Before Start; turn it on in the cruise and it is PASSING 10,000 FT CLIMB (which runs itself if the seat that reads it is on AUTO). Let the flight run past an offer nobody answered and the offer moves on with it.

**One after another.** Checklists that share a moment are offered in the book's order, each after the one before has been started or declined: a sensor cannot tell PREFLIGHT's checklists apart, nor After Start from Before Taxi.

**Passing.** Starting or declining a checklist passes it and every checklist before it. Starting a checklist from the Documents index does the same: start Before Start without the preflight checklists and the crew moves on to Starting Engines.

**On the ground, in order.** On the ground the crew also reads the ticks. A checklist already complete is passed without being offered, and nothing is offered while the checklist before it on the card is incomplete ([Where the offers stop](#offers-stop)). In the air this does not apply: a phase of flight does not wait for a box to be ticked.

**The 10,000 ft checklists.** With the seat that reads them on AUTO (the S/O, the FE, the MD-10's F/O) the PASSING 10,000 FT checklists start themselves, with no bubble, and that crew member works them through. Otherwise they are offered like the rest.

**The turnaround.** When Leaving Aircraft has been started or declined, the next flight's PREFLIGHT is offered after a ten-minute turnaround. If you shut down and then start an engine again without answering Leaving Aircraft (neither Start nor Not Now), the next leg's checklists resume at once at Starting Engines, PREFLIGHT and Before Start being behind an engine already turning.
**The last flight's ticks.** After the turnaround the previous flight's ticks no longer count as complete. Untick and redo a checklist, or Start it, which clears it.
**A new aircraft** (a variant change or a reload) starts the card again from the beginning.

blocks.content: The tanker's local pattern checklists and its non-standard Power Off Cocking and Scramble procedures are never offered; start them from the index when you need them.
The MD-10's EXTERIOR INSPECTION is the captain's alone and is never offered.

After a Not Now on No. 2 at Starting Engines, the engines-running moment counts two engines as enough, so After Start (DC-10) and Before Taxi are offered with No. 2 still to start. The allowance ends when No. 2 is running or every engine is shut down.

On the ground AUTO offers a checklist only when the one before it on the card is complete, every item ticked. A checklist that is left incomplete therefore stops the offers until you tick it through, or until you start the next checklist yourself from Documents. Expect this in these places:

items: After any checklist you declined with Not Now on the ground, or stopped before its end.
**After Landing** is not offered if Before Landing was declined or stopped in the air: the rule looks back across the landing.
**BEFORE START** waits for CAPT AND F/O PRE-FLIGHT, in which more than thirty of your items have nothing the crew can check and wait for your tick.
**COCKPIT PREPARATION** waits for PILOT'S INTERIOR INSPECTION, most of whose items are yours to tick.
**F/O COCKPIT PREPARATION** waits for CAPTAIN'S COCKPIT PREPARATION, which is offered in its turn although every item in it is yours and none is checked by the crew.

Side box 'Captain's only, never offered: Exterior Inspection'.
blocks.title: MD-10: which checklist is offered when

sections.title: A flight with the Virtual Crew
sections.summary: Every checklist from cold and dark to leaving the aircraft, when it is offered, what the crew does in it and what is left to you.

blocks.content: This section is the practical guide: a complete flight on your aircraft, checklist by checklist, with the crew on AUTO. Read it once before your first flight with the crew, and keep it open beside the EFB the first few times. The normal procedures behind each checklist, their amplification and their limits, are in Section 5 [Normal procedures](normal-procedures); this section says only who does what when the Virtual Crew is aboard. With the seats on MANUAL the flow is the same, except that you start each checklist yourself and tick every one of your items.

items: Each table lists every item of the checklist in the book's order. Items treated alike share a row only where they stand together in the book, except in the long preflight checklists, where like items are grouped; the run still takes them in their places.

**Answered**: the crew member answers in their turn with nothing moved (a look, a document, a test whose only result is a light). Where the book wants something set that the crew does not set, the row says so; [Items the crew answers without setting them](#answered-items) gathers them.
**Your tick**: the run waits for you. **AUTO: seen ...**: on AUTO the crew ticks your item when it sees the control in place; on MANUAL it waits for your tick.
A shared item is answered seat by seat: the systems seat, then the right seat, then you.

blocks.content: A crew member starting an engine checks only that it turns and runs. They do not read the start pressure first (the KC-10 FE excepted) or watch the EGT, and they answer the start, then begin the next, as soon as N2 passes 50 %, before the engine has settled at idle. Have air on the manifold and the ignition selected, watch each start as the captain does, and shut the fuel lever yourself on a hot or hung start ([Engines](engines), [Limitations](limitations)).

children.title: DC-10: cold and dark to shutdown

blocks.content: This is a whole DC-10 flight with both seats on AUTO, the way the Virtual Crew works it. It applies to every DC-10 variant: the passenger aircraft, the freighters, the air tankers, the Omega tanker and the KDC-10 all fly FedEx's card.

items: Load the aircraft cold and dark. In the Virtual Crew app set **Flight Engineer/Second Officer** and **First Officer** to AUTO. Set a **Target Cruise CG** now if you want the S/O to trim the CG in the cruise ([Cruise duties](#cruise-duties)).

Plan the flight and load fuel and payload in the EFB. Calculate the takeoff card on the Performance app's takeoff page before BEFORE START, with the AC and anti-ice you intend to use: every Start hands the crew the card as last calculated, and the S/O sets the takeoff bleeds and wing anti-ice from it, the F/O the engine anti-ice, and the F/O checks your flaps and stabilizer trim against it. Set Bugs also fills the checklist's flap, trim and gross weight blanks.

In Ground Ops, put the chocks in. The S/O will not release the parking brake without them, and asks for them to be removed at BEFORE TAXI. A ground power cart is optional: the S/O starts the APU, and asks for the cart only if the APU fails.
Keep an eye on the EFB: the crew's offers, calls and questions appear in the bubble over whatever app is open, and a stopped item shows in the run strip.

blocks.content: Parked with no engine running, AUTO offers the four PREFLIGHT checklists one after another. The first three are the S/O's; the fourth is the pilots'. Each is offered when the one before is complete.

blocks.title: INTERIOR SAFETY CHECK (S/O)
rows: Checked down and locked; otherwise stops: “The landing gear is not down and locked”
OFF (STBY if an engine is running: the antenna is damaged if switched off while moving)
Released, but only with the chocks in and no engine running; otherwise stops: “No chocks in: the parking brake stays set” or “An engine is running: the parking brake stays set”

blocks.title: COCKPIT INSPECTION (S/O)
rows: Consumables; Oxygen Pressure and Quantity; Oxygen Mask/Audio Panel; Courier Seat Oxygen Valve; FDAS; Cabin Air Shutoff Handle; Second Observer's Oxygen Mask; Gear Pins; First Observer Oxygen Mask/Audio Panel
Answered: the S/O does not align or load the INS. Do it yourself ([Navigation](navigation))
NO SMOKING on; SEAT BELTS pushed only if the sign is not already lit

blocks.title: SECOND OFFICER PRE-FLIGHT (S/O)
rows: Started: battery BAT, meter selector BAT & L EMER AC, APU/ISOL valve and crossfeeds closed, APU fuel pump on, master RUN, START about 20 s later for the inlet door, back to RUN; idle within 3.5 min or the start is terminated. Five seconds after it runs, the three APU GEN BUS switches on, two seconds apart; once all three generator buses are powered, the No. 2 right aft tank pump on and the APU fuel pump off. If it does not start, or its power does not reach the buses within 30 s, the S/O asks for ground power and ground air
ALL TEST held 5 s, then off

About half a minute: both RMPs OFF; AUX PUMP 1 (ADG) START and system 3 watched up; AUX PUMP 2 START; RUDDER STBY PWR ARM; 2-3 RMP ARM and system 2 watched up; 1-3 RMP ARM and system 1 watched up; both aux pumps STOP
Left pumps ON, right pumps AUTO
Each GEN switch RESET, then ON; the three AC BUS TIE switches NORM
DC TIE 1, DC TIE 3 and DC X-TIE OPEN

About forty seconds: every tank pump and the tank 2 transfer pump on in turn, then off; #2 crossfeed open, #1 and #3 open, #1 and #3 closed, #2 closed; the No. 2 right aft pump left on if the APU runs
All three ENG PNEU SUPPLY selectors OFF
OPEN, if the APU is running or a ground air cart is coupled
Cockpit and cabin zone selectors to AUTO, 75 °F
FWD and AFT CARGO FIRE TEST held 2 s each; CARGO FIRE switch TEST 2 s, then NORM; CABIN CARGO SMOKE TEST 2 s, then ARM on aircraft with a main cargo deck, OFF on the others
The four LOOPS selectors BOTH, one at a time; LOOP A and B TEST held 5 s
Cabin pressure control handle AUTO only. The landing altitude, barometric setting and rate are not set: set them yourself ([Air conditioning](air-conditioning))
CARGO DOOR INDICATION TEST held 2 s

Oxygen Switch; Fuel Manifold Drain & Outbd Fill; Fuel Quantity; Fuel Dump; Fuel Temperature; Fuel Filter Lights; Manifold Fail Lights; Annunciator Panel; Engine Instruments; Brake Temp System; Water System; Clock
Answered (the fuel quantity, manifold fail and brake temperature tests are not run)

blocks.content: When the APU fails, the S/O asks for ground power and ground air in the bubble ([When the crew calls or asks](#crew-calls)). Press Ground Ops and call the carts. As soon as the power cart is plugged in the S/O selects EXT PWR, checks the buses and carries on; the air cart feeds the packs and, later, the engine starts. If a cart is already plugged in when the APU fails, they do not ask: they select EXT PWR at once.

CAPT AND F/O PRE-FLIGHT has 70 items, below grouped by who does what. The run takes them in the book's order, and the book puts the captain's flows first: the F/O's first item of their own, Ground Prox and Radar, is the twenty-fifth. More than thirty of your items have nothing the crew can check, so the F/O's tests come only as you tick your way down. Tick ahead as you work your flow to keep the F/O moving.

blocks.title: CAPT AND F/O PRE-FLIGHT (F/O and you)
rows: Weather radar to TEST until the test pattern has painted through one full sweep (about 25 s from cold, at most 45 s), a look at the pattern, then OFF. Stops on “The radar test did not sweep” or “The radar test pattern is not all there”. The GPWS test is not run: do it yourself
The F/O's DME switch NORM, on the navigation fits that have one (the radio tests are not run)

Stall test L held until the columns shake and 3 s more, then R; overspeed warning test 1, then 2; speed control test SLOW, then FAST. No shaker within 10 s stops the run: “No stick shaker on the L stall test” (or R)
OFF (the current check through each position is not run)
The F/O's HSI to VOR; your tick
The F/O's flight director on; AUTO: yours seen on
The F/O's ADI TEST held 3 s; your tick
Gear light test held; gear handle pulled out of its detent (not up) for the red lights and the horn; HORN OFF; handle released. Stops “The gear handle is not down and in” if the gear is not down
Oxygen Mask/Audio Panel; Clocks; MACH/AS Indicators; Radio Alts; Altimeters; Marker Beacon Lights; RMI/HSI; VSI/TRA; INS Flight Plan
TAS/SAT Indicator; Thrust Rating Computer; Flaps/Slats Indicator; Surface Position Indicator; Flaps/Slats; ADG Handle

Flap Limit Override; Elevator Feel; ADG; Yaw Dampers; Anti-Skid; Ignition; Emergency Power; Emergency Lights; No Smoke & Seat Belt; Exterior Lights; Autopilots; Autothrottles; Spoiler; Fuel Levers; Aileron & Rudder Trim; Auto Brake System; DME Switch
AUTO: seen in the book's position

Annunciator Lights; Eng Fire Handle; Hydraulic Flight Control Lights; Aux Hyd Pumps (Start, Stop); Brakes; Stab Trim; INS; Compass; HF Radios; selectors; Voice Recorder; Fuel Vapor Vent; Standby Compass; Alt Preselect; Bank Angle; Speed Select; standby instruments; Reverser Lights; Engine Instruments; Takeoff Warning & Throttles; Transponder/TCAS

blocks.content: BEFORE START is offered once there is AC power on the buses and CAPT AND F/O PRE-FLIGHT is complete; if you leave any of your preflight items unticked, start BEFORE START yourself from Documents. Have the takeoff card calculated by now: the run hands it to the crew when it starts.

blocks.title: BEFORE START
rows: Yaw Dampers; Anti-Skid; Emergency Lights; Defog
AUTO: seen on, armed, armed, on
The S/O cannot set their regulator and stops: “S/O: OXY SUPPLY LEVER is not wired yet”. Tick the item
Hydraulic System; Battery Switch; Fuel Panel
CABIN CARGO SMOKE ARM on aircraft with a main cargo deck
F/O answers; your tick. Takeoff Data carries Go to Performance
The gross weight counter's zero-fuel setting dialed to the aircraft's zero-fuel weight, so the counter reads the gross weight
Every fitted cabin door's slide armed
AUTO: START A or START B seen selected
Set for start: the four aft boost pumps on, the packs off, the left engine hydraulic pumps OFF and the right ones AUTO

blocks.title: STARTING ENGINES (No. 3, No. 1, No. 2)
rows: Answered: the S/O does not read the start pressure

START switch engaged; fuel lever ON at 15 % N2; the switch drops out by itself at about 45 % N2; answered once N2 passes 50 %. No rotation to 15 % within a minute: the switch is released and the run stops, “No. 3 did not turn: check the start air”. Not past 50 % N2 within 90 s of fuel: “No. 3 did not reach idle”
Asks “Start No. 2 engine?”. Yes: started the same way. Not Now: the item is passed with No. 2 not running, FedEx's delayed engine start

blocks.content: AFTER START is offered when three engines are running (two after a Not Now on No. 2), then BEFORE TAXI. BEFORE TAKEOFF is offered once you are taxiing.

blocks.title: AFTER START
rows: AUTO: seen OFF; after a delayed No. 2, ticked with the ignition still on
AUTO: seen set. Set it before the ground crew are cleared
Left engine pumps ON and right OFF, until systems 1 and 3 hold 2,800 psi on the left pumps alone (up to 15 s); right pumps back to AUTO; both RMPs and RUDDER STBY PWR ARM
With No. 2 running: the three APU GEN BUS switches and EXT PWR off, the AC BUS TIEs NORM, PARALLEL GENS pushed and released, the buses checked. Then the meter selector to BAT & L EMER AC
The crew's normal configuration: the three ENG PNEU SUPPLY selectors AUTO, both isolation valves NORM, every pack AUTO

blocks.title: BEFORE TAXI
rows: S/O answers. F/O: engine anti-ice on if the takeoff card was computed with Eng or Eng+Wing, off otherwise; with no card, left as it is
Landing lights extended but not lit; nose light TAXI; runway turnoff lights on
S/O: with the chocks in or a cart still connected, asks “Ground equipment still at the aircraft. Have it removed.” and waits for them to go. AUTO: ticked once nothing is connected

blocks.title: BEFORE TAKEOFF
rows: If No. 2 is not running: ignition START A, No. 2 started as at Starting Engines, ignition OFF
Only if No. 2 was started after a delay and the APU is running: APU GEN BUS switches off, AC ties NORM, PARALLEL GENS, buses checked, APU OFF. Otherwise answered

You set them. The F/O waits up to 30 s for the surfaces to reach the card's FLAP with the slats out, then says “Flaps and slats are not at the takeoff setting.” and keeps waiting. AUTO then ticks your half
S/O answers; the F/O arms the spoilers
You trim. The F/O waits up to 20 s for the stabilizer within 0.3° of the card's STAB and aileron and rudder trim at zero, then says “Trim is not at the takeoff setting.”. AUTO then ticks your half
Aft boost pumps on, crossfeeds closed. With more than 40,000 lb in tank 2: its transfer pump on and the tank 1 and 3 fill valves open, feeding the wing tanks
AUTO: seen out of START (OFF, CONT A or CONT B)
F/O: weather radar on; your tick
ON, altitude reporting (TA/RA on the keypad transponder)
High-intensity lights on, landing lights on, nose light TAXI and LANDING, navigation lights on

From the card. Packs off: the three supplies and every pack OFF, a bleeds-off takeoff; with Eng+Wing anti-ice the supplies stay on for the wing and only the packs go off. Packs on, or no card: packs AUTO. The APU/ISOL valve closed either way
ON for an Eng+Wing card, OFF otherwise

blocks.content: The tank 2 transfer the S/O opens at BEFORE TAKEOFF is not closed by any later checklist item. With a cruise CG target set the S/O takes the fuel panel over in the cruise and manages it; without one, end the transfer yourself as the [Fuel](fuel) part describes.
AFTER TAKEOFF is offered climbing through 1,500 ft above the runway. If you start it earlier, on the runway, nothing happens until the gear call: the first item waits for 50 ft and a positive rate.

blocks.title: AFTER TAKEOFF
rows: At 50 ft with a positive rate: “Positive rate. Gear up.”; answered when the gear is up and locked. No call if it is already up
Watched behind the walk until the flap and slat surfaces are up (not just the handle); the walk goes on meanwhile
The normal pneumatic configuration: supplies AUTO, isolation valves NORM, packs AUTO. After a packs-off takeoff this is where the bleeds and packs come back
Answered: set them yourself as required

blocks.title: PASSING 10,000 FT CLIMB (runs itself with the S/O on AUTO)
rows: Off (the push pressed only if the sign is lit)

blocks.content: No checklist falls due in the cruise. Level at or above 20,000 ft for a minute with no checklist running, the S/O starts holding the cruise CG target if one is set, and on AUTO keeps the cabin zones between 65 and 75 °F whenever a pack is running ([Cruise duties](#cruise-duties)). The crew does nothing else between checklists: fuel balance, fuel temperature, pressurization and the rest of the panel are yours to watch.

IN RANGE is offered descending through 18,000 ft. Passing 10,000 ft on the way down the S/O's light checklist runs, then APPROACH is offered. BEFORE LANDING is offered below 2,500 ft above the runway.

blocks.title: IN RANGE
rows: F/O answers; your tick. Go to Performance opens the landing page
All seven tank pumps on, crossfeeds closed
Answered: set the landing altitude and barometric setting yourself

blocks.title: PASSING 10,000 FT DESCENT (runs itself with the S/O on AUTO)
APPROACH
rows: Answered: tune and set them yourself

blocks.title: BEFORE LANDING
rows: S/O answers. F/O: “Gear down.” if it is not; answered with every leg down and locked
S/O answers; the F/O arms them
Answered: select the landing mode yourself
S/O answers. F/O: “Flaps and slats for landing.” until the handle is in the landing range and the slats are out

children.title: After landing to leaving the aircraft

blocks.content: AFTER LANDING is offered below 40 kt on the ground, if BEFORE LANDING was completed ([Where the offers stop](#offers-stop)). SHUT DOWN is offered when you stop with the parking brake set, and LEAVING AIRCRAFT after it.

blocks.title: AFTER LANDING
rows: Landing lights and high-intensity lights off, nose light TAXI
Answered: the selector is not moved. Turn the probe heat off yourself
Handle to UP/RET; answered when the surfaces are up. Not up within two minutes: “The flaps and slats did not retract”
Trimmed to 2° ANU with the pedestal trim handle, held until the stabilizer gets there
Answered: the switches are not moved. Turn them off yourself
Started, unless a ground power cart is at the aircraft; its APU GEN BUS switches on. Not running within two minutes, the run stops: “S/O: it did not come in time”

blocks.content: The card puts the captain's shutdown items first and the S/O's silent items after them, so the S/O starts only when yours are answered. On AUTO, shut the engines down and set the switches; the crew ticks them as you go.

blocks.title: SHUT DOWN
rows: Landing, runway turnoff, nose and high-intensity lights off
Fuel Levers; Beacon; Seat Belt Sign; Emergency Lights; Windshield Anti-Ice; Defog; Engine Anti-Ice; Anti-Skid; INS
Dig EGT Memory & Eng Limit Pointers
All off, except the No. 2 right aft pump while the APU runs
Pneu Supplies & Packs; APU/ISOL Valve Swt
CABIN CARGO SMOKE OFF, on aircraft with a main cargo deck

blocks.title: LEAVING AIRCRAFT
rows: Chocks put in through Ground Ops, and checked in. Not in within 10 s: “The chocks did not go in”
Released, on the chocks with no engine running
Pitot covers, then engine covers, on
Master OFF, APU fuel pump off

blocks.content: LEAVING AIRCRAFT ends the flight for the crew. Once it is answered, by Start or by Not Now, the crew waits ten minutes and then offers INTERIOR SAFETY CHECK for the next flight. For a quick turn with the aircraft kept powered, leave the LEAVING AIRCRAFT offer unanswered instead: run BEFORE START and STARTING ENGINES yourself from Documents, and once an engine is running again AUTO carries on with AFTER START ([Turnaround procedure](ground-operations#turnaround-procedure)).

children.title: KC-10: cold and dark to shutdown

blocks.content: A KC-10 flight with the flight engineer and copilot on AUTO, following the -1's normal procedures. The three preflight inspections, which run to well over a hundred items, are summarized by what the FE moves; the other tables give every item. The boom operator's items are answered by the FE. The air refueling procedures have no crew items: the boom, the centerline drogue and the wing pods are yours (or the boom operator station's) to work ([Air refueling systems](air-refueling-systems)).

items: Load the aircraft cold and dark and set **Flight Engineer** and **Copilot** to AUTO in the Virtual Crew app.

Calculate the takeoff card in Performance before COCKPIT PREPARATION, whose first item links to it: the FE sets the takeoff packs and bleeds and the wing anti-ice from the card, the copilot the engine anti-ice, and both check your flaps and trim against it.
The FE personally puts the chocks in and takes the covers off during their initial inspection, and starts the APU. The FE asks for carts only when needed.

blocks.content: Parked with no engine running, AUTO offers the FE's three inspections and the pilot's interior inspection in the -1's order, each when the one before is complete.

blocks.title: FE'S EXTERIOR/INTERIOR INITIAL INSPECTION: what the FE moves
rows: Chocks put in through Ground Ops if they are not in. Not in within 10 s: “The chocks did not go in”
Pitot covers, then engine covers, removed
Battery BAT and locked; meter selector BAT & L EMER AC
Checked down; otherwise “The landing gear is not down and locked”
APU and Engine Fire Detection System
LOOPS selectors BOTH; LOOP A and B TEST held 5 s

APU GEN BUS switches off, APU/ISOL valve closed, the APU's fuel from the APU fuel pump (from tank 2's right aft pump if AC is already on the buses), master RUN, START about 20 s later, back to RUN; idle within 3.5 min. If it does not start: “The APU did not start” (tick the item; the next item asks for ground power)

APU GEN BUS switches on, five seconds after the APU runs and two seconds apart; then the APU's fuel from tank 2's right aft pump and the APU fuel pump off. With no APU power: “No APU. Call for ground power and ground air.” (or “APU power did not come on line ...”), then EXT PWR once the cart is plugged in
Both motor pumps cycled ARM and OFF; RUDDER STBY PWR ARM; AUX PUMP 1 START (system 3 up), AUX PUMP 2 START; 2-3 then 1-3 motor pumps ARM, each system watched up; engine pumps left OFF, right AUTO
Each system's MANFLD FAIL light held with the valves set for it, the tripped supply reset through OFF to AUTO; system 2 on APU air; the 1-3 isolation valve back to NORM
With the APU or a ground air cart: APU/ISOL valve open, packs 1 and 3 AUTO, temperature selectors AUTO
All three on, one at a time
All three to NAV, one at a time

blocks.title: FE'S INTERIOR INSPECTION: what the FE moves
rows: AUTO; MAN with the slew to INCR, back to center, to DECR, back to center; AUTO again (REF IAS back to the white band)
The four YAW DAMP switches on; the test pushed and its 20 s watched
ON; after 3 s the meter selector to BAT & L EMER AC; OFF 3 s later
TERR OVRD, STEEP APPR and FLAP OVRD off; GPWS TEST pressed and its callouts heard out
Stall Warning System; Max Speed Warn System; Speed Control
Stall test L held until the columns shake and 3 s more, then R; overspeed warning test 1, then 2; speed control SLOW, then FAST. No shaker within 10 s: “No stick shaker on the L stall test” (or R)
NORM if in icing conditions; defog ON
Stepped through every position, each probe's current read, then OFF
HI-INT off, navigation lights full bright, nose light off, landing lights retracted
Pilot's Annunciator Lights; Pilot's Instrument Panel
ANNUN LT TEST held 3 s; both static selectors NORMAL
Gear handle pulled (red, horn), HORN OFF, released. Stops if the gear is not down
Released for the horn test, only on chocks with no engine running (the takeoff warning horn test itself is not run)
Each generator RESET then ON; AC BUS TIEs NORM; DC TIEs and X-TIE OPEN; battery BAT and locked; meter selector BAT & L EMER AC
Supplies 1 and 3 AUTO, wing anti-ice OFF, packs AUTO, temperature selectors AUTO, avionic flow NORM, trim air on, lav/galley vent on
Each aft pump on and read, then off (tank 2's right aft left on for a running APU); fuel used reset
Hydraulic Motor Pump Sws; Auxiliary Hydraulic Pumps
Motor pumps OFF; aux pumps stopped
The FE's regulator SUPPLY ON and 100 %, EMERGENCY held 3 s, NORMAL, SUPPLY OFF
Answered. Among them SEAT BELTS Sw (AUTO), IFF/ETCAS (STBY) and Pressurization (SET) are not set

blocks.content: **FE'S EXTERIOR INSPECTION** is a walkaround with nothing to move: the FE answers each item. **PILOT'S INTERIOR INSPECTION** is yours and the copilot's, and most of its items are shared: the copilot answers, then the run waits for your tick. The copilot's own work comes only as you tick your way down, so tick ahead. They run their oxygen regulator check (supply on, 100 %, emergency, normal, off), switch their flight director on and run their weather radar test: TEST, then the pattern watched behind the walk while the tanker's transmitter warms up (about three minutes from power-on), STBY once a full sweep has been seen. They answer their other items. On AUTO your flight director, autothrottle and autopilot lever items are ticked when seen set; the rest wait for your tick.

children.title: Cockpit preparation, before start and engine start

blocks.content: COCKPIT PREPARATION is offered once there is power and PILOT'S INTERIOR INSPECTION is complete; if you leave items of it unticked, start COCKPIT PREPARATION yourself from Documents.

blocks.title: COCKPIT PREPARATION
rows: Crew answers; your tick. Go to Performance opens the takeoff page
FE and copilot each set their regulator SUPPLY ON and 100 %; AUTO: yours seen on and 100 %
Copilot's compass SLAVED; AUTO: yours seen slaved
The four YAW DAMP switches on, one at a time
Answered (tested in the FE's interior inspection)
FE answers. Copilot: navigation lights full bright

blocks.title: BEFORE START
rows: FE turns any MSU not at NAV to NAV; copilot answers; AUTO: all seen at NAV
The aft pumps of tanks 1, 2 (both) and 3 on, one at a time
Packs 1 and 3 PACK OFF (the KC-10 has no pack 2)
AUTO: START A or B seen selected

With neither the APU nor a ground air cart: “No air for the start. Call for ground air.” Then APU/ISOL valve open and 25 psi looked for on PRESS gauge 1 or 3; if short, supplies 1 and 3 OFF and looked for again; still short: “Pneumatic pressure is below 25 psi”
CARGO DOOR INDICATION TEST held 2 s
Cabin Doors Lights; Before Start Checklist

blocks.title: STARTING ENGINES (No. 3, No. 1, No. 2)
rows: At least 25 psi on PRESS gauge 1 or 3 within 10 s; otherwise “Start pressure is below 25 psi”
You start them: start switch, fuel lever ON at 15 % N2. AUTO: answered as each passes 50 % N2
Asks “Start No. 2 engine now?”. Yes: ignition to START A if not in START, start switch, fuel lever at 15 % N2, answered once N2 passes 50 %. Not Now: passed, to be started during the taxi
The three left engine pumps ON; each running engine's system watched to 2,800 psi; otherwise “An engine's hydraulic system is below 2800 psi”

blocks.title: BEFORE TAXI
rows: FE: wing anti-ice on for an Eng+Wing card, off otherwise (no card: left alone). Copilot: engine anti-ice as the card says; with no card, on in icing conditions (below 6 °C in visible moisture)
Left engine pumps ON, right AUTO, 2-3 motor pump ARM
Supplies 1 and 3 AUTO, both isolation valves NORM, packs 1 and 3 AUTO, one at a time
FE: with chocks or a cart still connected, “Ground equipment still at the aircraft. Have it removed.” AUTO: ticked once all is clear

blocks.title: BEFORE TAKEOFF
rows: You set them. The FE, then the copilot, check the surfaces against the card's FLAP with the slats out (30 s, then “Flaps and slats are not at the takeoff setting.”); AUTO ticks yours
You trim. FE, then copilot, check stabilizer within 0.3° of the card and aileron and rudder at zero (20 s, then “Trim is not at the takeoff setting.”); AUTO ticks yours
You arm them; AUTO: seen armed
If No. 2 is not running: started as at Starting Engines, then ignition OFF
RUDDER STBY PWR ARM, 2-3 and 1-3 motor pumps ARM, both aux pumps stopped

With three engines running: EXT PWR off, the APU GEN BUS switches off, AC BUS TIEs NORM, PARALLEL GENS pushed, the buses checked (“The engine generators did not take the buses” if not); meter selector BAT & L EMER AC
With three engines and every generator bus on engine power: APU/ISOL valve closed, APU master OFF
Supplies AUTO, APU/ISOL closed, isolation valves NORM; MANFLD FAIL 1 held (system 1 pressure decays), supply 1 reset through OFF; the same for system 3
From the card. Packs off: both packs OFF and both supplies OFF; with Eng+Wing anti-ice the supplies stay AUTO and wing anti-ice goes ON. Otherwise supplies AUTO and packs AUTO. APU/ISOL valve closed
Answered: the IFF is set on the CDUs, by you
High-intensity lights on, landing lights on, nose light TAXI and LANDING

blocks.title: AFTER TAKEOFF/CLIMB
rows: Copilot: at 50 ft with a positive rate, “Positive rate. Gear up.”; answered when the gear is up
After a packs-off takeoff: supplies 1 and 3 AUTO, then packs 1 and 3 AUTO, one at a time
Watched behind the walk until the surfaces are up
Boom Operator/Exterior Lights & Seat Belt Sw
FE: runway turnoff lights off (the seat belt switch is not moved); your tick

blocks.title: PASSING 10,000 FT CLIMB (runs itself with the FE on AUTO)
rows: Answered: the tanker's seat belt switch is not moved by the crew

blocks.content: In the cruise the FE, on AUTO, keeps the cabin zones between 65 and 75 °F ([Cabin temperature](#cabin-temperature)). There is no cruise CG management on the KC-10: its body tanks and transfers are yours ([Fuel](fuel)).

blocks.title: DESCENT (offered descending through 18,000 ft)
rows: Copilot answers; your tick. Go to Performance opens the landing page
Answered: set the landing altitude yourself

blocks.title: PASSING 10,000 FT DESCENT (runs itself with the FE on AUTO)
APPROACH
rows: Every tank pump on, one at a time; crossfeeds closed
Copilot selects GA, but not above 14,000 ft: started higher, the copilot watches for 14,000 ft behind the walk

blocks.title: BEFORE LANDING
rows: FE answers; copilot: “Gear down.” until down and locked; AUTO ticks yours
You arm them; AUTO: seen armed
ANTI-SKID ARM (the test is not run)
FE answers; copilot: “Flaps and slats for landing.” until in the landing range; AUTO ticks yours

children.title: After landing to leaving the aircraft

blocks.title: AFTER LANDING
rows: Radar STBY (the IFF is the CDUs')
Unless a ground power cart is at the aircraft: tank 2's right aft pump on, APU started as in the initial inspection, APU GEN BUS switches on. No start within 3.5 min: “The APU did not start”
High-intensity and landing lights off, nose light TAXI
Wing anti-ice OFF; engine anti-ice OFF unless in icing conditions (below 6 °C in visible moisture)
You retract them; AUTO: seen retracted
Handle UP/RET, answered when the surfaces are up (“The flaps and slats did not retract” after two minutes). In icing conditions the copilot leaves them for you
Stabilizer trimmed to 2° nose up with the pedestal handle

Motor pumps OFF; left engine pumps OFF for 5 s and each running system checked at 2,800 psi on the right pumps, left pumps ON; then right pumps OFF and checked on the left pumps, right back to AUTO. A short pump stops the run: “A right engine pump is below 2800 psi” (or left)
Asks “Shut down No. 2 engine?”. Yes: No. 2 fuel lever OFF, then tank 2's forward and left aft pumps off, the right aft on for a running APU

blocks.title: PARKING - ENGINE SHUTDOWN
rows: Chocks put in through Ground Ops; only if they do not come, AUX PUMP 1 started for the brakes
APU running: the three APU GEN BUS switches on. Otherwise: “No APU. Call for ground power.”, then EXT PWR and the AC ties NORM
FE answers. Copilot: landing, nose, runway turnoff and high-intensity lights off; beacon mast OFF once every engine has run down, or after a minute
Every tank pump off except tank 2's right aft for a running APU; crossfeeds closed

blocks.title: LEAVING AIRCRAFT
rows: FE: MSU 3 OFF; copilot: MSU 2 OFF; AUTO: all seen off
OFF (STBY if an engine still runs)
IFF Mode 4 Codes; FMS Radio Master Power
FE and copilot: SUPPLY OFF, 100 %; AUTO: yours seen off
APU/ISOL valve closed, master OFF; once it has run down, its fuel pumps off and the APU GEN BUS switches off
OFF, but only with the APU stopped (it powers the APU's fire detection)
Chocks in if none; pitot and engine covers on

blocks.content: AUTO never offers these; start them from the Documents index.

items: **FULL STOP TAXI BACK, DOWNWIND, BEFORE LANDING (pattern):** the crew answers its own items with nothing moved, makes no gear or flap calls, and your items wait for your tick. Set the radar, lights, thrust computer, flap selector and seat belt switch yourself.

**POWER OFF COCKING:** FE puts the chocks in; AUTO checks your parking brake released; FE turns the CDUs and MSU 3 off and the copilot MSU 2, AUTO checks every MSU off; emergency lights OFF; packs held at MAN HOT for 10 s, then PACK OFF; the outflow valve is not closed; APU shut down; battery off (only with the APU stopped); meter selector APU; every cabin and cargo door closed.

**SCRAMBLE:** FE takes the covers off, puts the meter selector to BAT & L EMER AC and the battery on, starts the APU or uses a cart (asking for ground power if neither), sets the outflow valve AUTO and the packs on APU or cart air, turns the CDUs on and the MSUs to NAV; pressurizes all three hydraulic systems (aux pumps and motor pumps; “Hydraulic pressure did not come up” if not); as the boom operator, AR MASTER PWR on and HYD SEL to BOOM for two minutes, then off with the hydraulic pumps; removes the chocks once your parking brake is set; closes every working cabin door and arms the slides. PARKING disarms them again.

children.title: MD-10: cold and dark to shutdown

blocks.content: An MD-10 flight with the first officer on AUTO, following FedEx's MD-10 FCOM. The F/O reads every checklist on the ground and, as pilot not flying, in the air. The overhead's systems controllers stay in AUTO throughout; the book's [MANUAL] steps are worked only for a panel whose SYSTEM selector you have put to MANUAL, and then only where the table says so.

items: Load the aircraft cold and dark and set **First Officer** to AUTO in the Virtual Crew app.
Put the chocks in through Ground Ops: with them in, the F/O releases a set parking brake at their safety inspection; without them the F/O leaves it set, and stops if it is off.

Calculate the takeoff card in Performance before FINAL COCKPIT PREPARATION: the F/O dials the FLAP T.O. selector from it, sets the anti-ice and the takeoff packs and bleeds from it, and checks your flaps and stabilizer against it.

blocks.title: COCKPIT SAFETY INSPECTION (F/O, before power)
rows: Checked off; otherwise “A fuel lever is not off”
With chocks in: a set brake released, if no engine is running. Without chocks: left set; if it is off, “No chocks in and the parking brake is off”
Checked: spoiler handle retracted and disarmed, flap/slat handle agreeing with the surfaces. Otherwise stops with what is wrong
Checked down; otherwise “The gear handle is not down”
Fuel Dump and Manifold Drain Switches
Checked off; otherwise “The fuel dump switch is not off”

blocks.title: PRELIMINARY COCKPIT PREPARATION (F/O)
rows: With a ground power cart plugged in: EXT PWR pushed and the buses checked (“External power did not come on line” if not). No cart: answered
Engine/APU Fire Test - AC Buses Powered
With AC power: the four LOOPS switches BOTH; LOOP A and B TEST held; MASTER WARNING pushed to silence the bell; test released. Without AC: answered
Engine/APU Fire Test - Battery Power Only
On battery alone: the test held 5 s (lights only, no bell), then watched behind the walk until AC is on the buses, when the AC test is repeated

START/STOP pushed; running within 3.5 min, or pushed off again and “The APU did not start”. Unless a cart has the buses, APU PWR pushed five seconds later and the buses checked (“APU power did not come on line” if not)

blocks.content: **CAPTAIN'S COCKPIT PREPARATION** is offered next and is entirely yours: glareshield, oxygen, source selectors, displays, clock, IRS position, radio and audio panels. None of its items is checked by the crew, so tick each one as you do it. The F/O's own preparation is offered only once yours is complete; if you would rather not tick through it, start F/O COCKPIT PREPARATION from Documents.

blocks.title: F/O COCKPIT PREPARATION
rows: With the APU running or ground air: both ISOL valves on, the three packs on, zone temperature AUTO (the APU air and ECON switches are not pressed). With neither: “No APU or ground air: the packs stay off”

IRS 1, AUX and 2 to NAV one at a time; the first out of OFF runs the cargo fire test. If it does not appear, the manual CARGO FIRE TEST is held until it does (“The cargo fire test did not come” after 5 s)
Both igniter selections out: IGN OFF

In AUTO: answered (the pressure test is not run). In MANUAL: aux pump 1 on and system 3 checked, aux pump 2 on, each RMP on with its system checked and off again, both aux pumps off; a system that does not pressurize stops the run
Emergency power selector to ARM (stops “The AC buses are not powered” on a dead aircraft)
Answered, in AUTO and in MANUAL alike: the fuel panel check is not run
SEAT BELTS on (NO SMOKE is yours)
Set for the gate: landing lights retracted, nose light off, runway turnoff and wing lights off, navigation lights on, high-intensity off, beacon off while nothing turns
TERRAIN OVRD off; GPWS switch to TEST momentarily (guard lifted and closed); the callouts heard out
Checked FLAP LIMIT and ELEV FEEL in AUTO; otherwise “Flap limit or elevator feel is not in AUTO”
The four YAW DAMP switch-lights on, one at a time, if not already engaged
Gear Warning System and SD CONFIG Synoptic
Gear handle pulled out of its detent (never up) for 3 s, red on the panel and the synoptic, released
ARM, guard closed (the test is not run)

On the ground, no engine turning, AC up: thrust lever 1 full forward until the warning sounds, back to idle; then levers 2 and 3. Stops with what was wrong (“No takeoff warning on throttle 1”, “An engine is running: the throttles stay at idle”)
GAIN CAL, TEST; the pattern watched behind the walk through the transmitter's warm-up; SYS pressed and the other system tested the same way; OFF
ALT RPT on, mode STBY (the TCAS test is not run)
Checked at zero; otherwise “The rudder or aileron trim is not at zero” (the trims are yours)

The remaining items (IRS initialization, voice recorder, bus fault panel, AIR control panel, start panel, pressurization, anti-ice panel, fuel used, glareshield, oxygen, source selector, displays, clock, standby instruments, status page, radio panels, audio, ADG handle)

blocks.title: FINAL COCKPIT PREPARATION
rows: F/O dials the takeoff card's FLAP (with no card it is left to you); your tick
F/O answers; AUTO ticks yours as not installed (the MD-10 has no autobrake selector)

children.title: Cockpit preparation, before start and engine start

blocks.title: COCKPIT PREPARATION
rows: In MANUAL, the pump check as in the F/O's preparation; in AUTO answered
Answered, in MANUAL too: the fuel panel check is not run
Set for the gate, as in the F/O's preparation
F/O dials the card's FLAP; your tick (the blank fills from Set Bugs)
F/O answers; AUTO ticks yours as not installed

blocks.title: BEFORE START
rows: AUTO: IGN A or B seen selected
In MANUAL: tank 1, 2 and 3 pumps on; in AUTO answered
Set for start: both ISOL valves on, the three packs off, the three engine bleeds off

blocks.title: STARTING ENGINES (No. 3, No. 1, No. 2)
rows: Checks the thrust levers at idle (“A throttle is not at idle” otherwise); START pulled; FUEL lever ON at 15 % N2; the switch pops in by itself at about 45 % N2; answered once N2 passes 50 %, allowing up to two and a half minutes from fuel on for a cold start. No rotation in a minute: “No. 3 did not turn: check the start air”
The same, in turn. There is no question about No. 2 on the MD-10

blocks.title: AFTER START
rows: Engine anti-ice and wing anti-ice on or off as the takeoff card was computed; with no card, left as they are
With all three engines running: ISOL valves off, engine bleeds on, packs on. Otherwise “Not every engine is running: the air panel stays set for start”
START/STOP pushed and the APU shuts down. Only with all three engines running (“Not every engine is running: the APU stays on”)
In MANUAL: aux pumps and RMPs off, each left pump off in turn with the right pumps checked to hold 2,800 psi, left pumps back on. In AUTO answered
AUTO: ticked once no chocks, carts or ground power remain

blocks.title: TAXI
rows: You set them. The F/O checks the surfaces against the card's FLAP with the slats out (30 s, then “Flaps and slats are not at the takeoff setting.”); AUTO ticks yours
F/O arms the spoilers; AUTO ticks yours
You trim. The F/O checks the stabilizer within 0.3° of the card's STAB (20 s, then “Stabilizer trim is not at the takeoff setting.”); AUTO ticks yours

blocks.title: BEFORE TAKEOFF
rows: F/O: landing lights out and on, nose light TAXI and LANDING, high-intensity on; AUTO ticks yours
In MANUAL: 1-3 and 2-3 RMPs on; in AUTO answered
From the card. Packs off: packs off and, unless wing anti-ice is wanted, engine bleeds off. Otherwise bleeds and packs on

blocks.title: AFTER TAKEOFF (silent, the PNF's)
rows: At 50 ft with a positive rate: “Positive rate. Gear up.”; answered when the gear is up. The F/O never raises the gear
Engine bleeds on, then packs on
Watched behind the walk until the surfaces are up; then the FLAP T.O. selector back to 0
In MANUAL: RMPs off; in AUTO answered
Answered, in MANUAL too: set the transfer pumps and fill valves yourself

sections.title: Cruise duties
sections.summary: The DC-10 second officer's cruise CG management by fuel transfer, the flight engineer's cabin temperature control, and what the crew does not watch.

blocks.content: Between checklists the crew moves nothing, with two exceptions, both the flight engineer's and both continuous duties rather than checklist items. On the DC-10 the second officer holds a cruise CG you set, by transferring fuel between the main tanks. On the DC-10 and KC-10, with their seat on AUTO, the flight engineer keeps the cabin temperature in a comfortable band. The CG management gives way to checklists: while any run is under way the S/O lets go of the fuel panel. The cabin temperature control carries on through checklists, on the ground as in the air, whenever a pack is running.

**Why the CG matters in the cruise.** On a conventional airliner the wing's lift acts behind the center of gravity, so the wing on its own pitches the aircraft nose down; the horizontal tail balances it by pushing down. That download is weight the wing has to carry on top of the aircraft's own, and every pound of extra lift costs induced drag on the wing, while the tail's own lift costs drag on the tail. Together they are the **trim drag**. Moving the CG aft shortens the arm between the CG and the wing's lift, reduces the download needed, and with it the trim drag and the fuel burned. The price is stability: the further aft the CG, the closer it comes to the aircraft's neutral point, the lighter the stick forces and the more sensitive the aircraft in pitch, which is why the aft limit exists. A cruise CG near the aft part of the permitted range, but not at its edge, is the efficient place to be.

**Why it drifts.** In normal tank-to-engine operation each engine feeds from its own main tank, so two thirds of the fuel burned comes from tanks 1 and 3 in the wings. Because the wing is swept, the wing tanks' fuel lies well aft of the CG, roughly at the middle of the mean aerodynamic chord, while tank 2 in the center wing lies near its leading edge. Burning wing fuel therefore moves the CG forward through the flight. In FedEx's normal fuel management tank 2 is drawn down into tanks 1 and 3, which stay full until the three are even; that keeps the wing's bending relief and moves fuel aft. The S/O's CG management uses exactly those transfers, and their reverse, steered by the CG rather than by the tank quantities.

blocks.alt: Plan-view schematic of the DC-10-30 main fuel tanks with the CG scale: tank 1 (left wing) and tank 3 (right wing) each split into inboard and outboard compartments, tank 2 in the center wing split into left and right halves. A %MAC scale along the fuselage shows tank 2 near the front of the MAC and the wing tanks' centroids near mid-chord. Two colored arrow sets: orange 'Moving aft' from tank 2 (transfer pump) through the open fill valves into the inboard compartments of tanks 1 and 3; blue 'Moving forward' from tanks 1 and 3 (both wing transfer pumps) through the tank 2 fill valve into tank 2's left half. Crossfeed valves drawn closed. A small inset shows the CG moving aft or forward along the scale with the band: target, ±1.0 %MAC act band, ±0.3 %MAC hold band.
blocks.title: The S/O's CG transfers
blocks.caption: Tank 2 into tanks 1 and 3 moves the CG aft; tanks 1 and 3 into tank 2 moves it forward. The crossfeeds stay closed throughout.

blocks.content: In the Virtual Crew app, **Target Cruise CG** → **Set** turns the target on at the present CG rounded to half a percent; **−** and **+** move it in 0.5 %MAC steps; **Off** removes it. The target can be set anywhere from 8.0 to 30.0 %MAC, which runs from the FedEx Flight Manual's most forward CG limit to just inside its most aft. The envelope itself narrows with weight and series, and the target is not checked against it: choose a target inside the limits for your weights ([Limitations](limitations), [Mission planning](mission-planning)). Under the label the app shows the CG now and what the S/O is doing.

The CG the S/O works to is the aircraft's actual CG as it flies, computed from its loads and its fuel tank by tank, and shown as real %MAC. It is not the weight and balance figure measured on the ground, which does not change in flight.

children.title: When and how the S/O transfers

blocks.content: The S/O works the CG only when all of these hold: a target is set; their seat is on MANUAL or AUTO; no checklist run is under way; and the aircraft is in the cruise, airborne at or above 20,000 ft with less than 500 ft/min of vertical speed, continuously for a minute. Anything else and they let go: a transfer they started is stopped, every transfer pump off and every fill valve closed.

The control is deliberately loose, as a crew member's would be. The S/O leaves the CG alone while it is within **1.0 %MAC** of the target. Beyond that they start a transfer, and run it until the CG is back within **0.3 %MAC**, for at least 30 seconds. The two bands give hysteresis: a CG reading that wanders at the edge of the band cannot start and stop the pumps every few seconds, and a transfer once started moves enough fuel to be worth it.

blocks.content: Auxiliary tanks, where the aircraft has them, are not part of the S/O's CG management: transfers from them are yours ([Fuel](fuel)).

children.title: Sharing the fuel panel with the S/O

blocks.content: With a target set and the aircraft in the cruise, the S/O owns the main tank transfers. They write the transfer pumps and fill valves whenever the S/O's state changes (starting a transfer, ending one, taking the panel over), and close the crossfeeds whenever they start a transfer, so a transfer or a crossfeed you set up by hand meanwhile will be undone at the S/O's next change. To manage the fuel yourself, for an imbalance, a leak or a fuel temperature problem, set the target **Off** first. The S/O stops any transfer they started on letting go, and from then on leaves the panel alone.

The target is a CG, not a fuel plan. The S/O does not check the CG against the weight-dependent limits, does not keep fuel for landing CG, and does not manage lateral balance beyond stopping at 1,500 lb. Check the CG and the tank quantities on the FE panel through the cruise as the Fuel part describes.

With their seat on **AUTO** and at least one pack delivering air, the flight engineer keeps each cabin zone between **65 and 75 °F** with the zone temperature selectors on the air-conditioning panel: on the DC-10 the FWD, MID and AFT cabin zones, on the KC-10 the two cabin zone selectors its panel carries. The cockpit zone is the pilots' and is left alone. On MANUAL the flight engineer does not touch the zone selectors.

items: Each zone's temperature is read as the panel's indicator shows it.
A zone warmer than 75 °F has its selector moved one SET detent cooler (5 °F); one colder than 65 °F one detent warmer. A zone inside the band is left alone.
The flight engineer moves any one zone's selector at most once every two minutes, and watches for two minutes before the first move.
A zone is touched only while its selector is on the SET arc. A selector you have turned to MAN or STOP is yours, and stays yours until you put it back on the arc.
The SET arc runs from 65 to 85 °F; at its coldest detent there is nothing more to give.

blocks.content: **Why so slowly.** A cabin is a large thermal mass: after a change of selection the zone temperature takes several minutes to settle. A controller that acted faster than the cabin answered would overshoot and hunt from one end of the band to the other. One detent is half the width of the band, so a single step brings a zone from just outside the band to well inside it, and the two-minute pause lets each step take effect before the next is judged. On the APU alone, on a hot day, the packs may not have the air to reach the selected temperature at all: the cabin stays warm, and the flight engineer keeps stepping each zone cooler until it reaches 65 °F, which asks the packs for all the cooling they can give. That is the setting a line crew would choose, arrived at by the same rule.

blocks.alt: DC-10-30 flight engineer's air-conditioning panel area, close-up of the zone temperature control row: the COCKPIT, FWD CABIN, MID CABIN and AFT CABIN selectors with their STOP, MAN COLD, the SET arc marked 65 to 85 °F, and MAN HOT positions, each with its zone temperature indicator above. FWD and AFT selectors at the 70 °F detent, MID at 65, COCKPIT at 75. Packs 1, 2 and 3 in AUTO visible at the edge.
blocks.title: Zone temperature selectors
blocks.caption: The flight engineer works the cabin selectors on the SET arc only, one detent at a time. The cockpit selector is the pilots'.

children.title: What the crew does not watch

blocks.content: A real flight engineer spends the cruise watching their panel: fuel burn against the plan, balance, fuel temperature, generator loads, pressures, cabin altitude and rate. The virtual crew does not. Outside its checklists and the two duties above it neither scans the panels nor calls out anything it sees, and it takes no action on a caution or a warning. Keep the scan yourself: the EFB's [Systems app](efb#systems-app) and the panels show everything the crew would have been watching, and the failure procedures are in [Abnormal procedures](abnormal-procedures) and [Emergency procedures](emergency-procedures).

On the MD-10 the automatic systems controllers do much of that watching themselves, as they were designed to: they reconfigure fuel, hydraulics, air and electrics and alert you through the EAD and the system display. The first officer adds nothing to them in the cruise.

sections.title: Working with the crew
sections.summary: When your inputs and the crew's meet: what the crew will set again, what it leaves alone, and how to take an item, a seat or a duty over.

blocks.content: The crew's hand on a switch is a hand, not a lock. When an item calls for a switch the crew member moves it once to the position the item wants and lets go; they do not hold it there, and they do not come back to it unless a later item calls for the same switch. Anything you move between items stays where you put it until then. And because every crew item acts on the aircraft as it finds it, an item you have already done costs nothing: the APU is not restarted if it is running, an engine already turning is not started again, the seat belt push is pressed only if the sign is off, the MSUs are turned only if they are not at NAV.

children.title: What the crew will set again

blocks.content: Some switches are set by more than one checklist, and each time the crew sets them to that checklist's position whatever you chose in between. Expect these:

blocks.content: Two duties are continuous rather than per item, and they come back to their switches on their own. The DC-10 S/O's **cruise CG management** writes the main tank transfer pumps and fill valves whenever a transfer starts or ends, and closes the crossfeeds when one starts, and the **cabin temperature** control moves a cabin zone selector on the SET arc at most every two minutes. Turn the CG target Off, and put a zone selector to MAN or STOP (or the flight engineer's seat to MANUAL), to keep those switches yours.

The flight-path controls are yours, and the crew calls for them rather than moving them: the gear, the flaps and slats before landing, the takeoff flaps and trim, the thrust levers once the engines are running, the autopilot and autothrottle, and the parking brake for taxi and takeoff. The books do hand a few of them to a crew member at particular moments, and the crew moves them then:

items: **Parking brake:** released at the interior safety check (DC-10), the cockpit safety inspection (MD-10) and LEAVING AIRCRAFT (DC-10), but only with the chocks in and no engine running. The KC-10 FE releases it for their horn test and sets it again at their interior inspection.

**Start switches and fuel levers:** during STARTING ENGINES, by the F/O (DC-10, MD-10) or the FE for No. 2 (KC-10), and at BEFORE TAKEOFF for a delayed No. 2 (DC-10, KC-10); the KC-10 FE also shuts No. 2 down after landing if you say Yes.

**Thrust levers (MD-10 only):** moved forward and back by the F/O during the takeoff warning test, on the ground with no engine turning.
**Gear handle:** pulled out of its detent, never raised, for the gear warning test. No crew item can raise the gear.

sections.title: Abnormal and emergency operation
sections.summary: The crew works the normal checklists only: what it does when the aircraft is not normal, and what to do with it in a non-normal situation.

blocks.content: The Virtual Crew works only the normal checklists in Documents. It does not run any abnormal or emergency procedure, does not recognize a failure as such, and does not take any memory action. Section 2 [Emergency procedures](emergency-procedures) and Section 3 [Abnormal procedures](abnormal-procedures) are flown by you, with the crew's switches where the normal checklists left them.

What the crew does notice is an item it cannot complete. Every crew item checks the result it is after, so a failure that stands in the way of an item stops the run there with a plain statement of what did not happen. That makes the crew a useful, if narrow, detector on the ground: an APU that will not take the buses, an engine that will not turn, a stall warning that does not shake, a radar that does not paint its test, flaps that will not retract. The crew reads the aircraft's real state for these (an engine's own N2, the gear legs' own lock state), so a failed indicator does not mislead it; a real failure does stop it.

items: When a non-normal situation arises during a run, **Pause** or **Stop** the run before you work the procedure. A running item will otherwise go on moving switches while you work.

With a seat on AUTO the offers carry on following the flight. If the procedure takes you off the normal profile (a return, a diversion, an engine shut down), decline offers that no longer apply with Not Now, or set the seats to MANUAL until you are back on the normal checklists.
On the DC-10, set the Target Cruise CG to **Off** for any fuel problem (imbalance, leak, fuel temperature, a tank that will not feed), so that the S/O's transfers do not work against yours.

Some crew items assume all three engines. With one not running, a few stop the run and wait for your tick (the MD-10's After Start Air Panel and APU: “Not every engine is running ...”), and others are simply passed (the DC-10 S/O parallels the generators and shuts the APU down at After Start only with No. 2 running; the KC-10 FE does so at Before Takeoff only with three engines). items: Every crew action is a real switch movement in the cockpit, through the same inputs as your own hand, and the systems answer it exactly as they answer you. Nothing is set behind the scenes.
The crew has no voices yet. Calls, requests and questions are written in the EFB's crew bubble, and stopped items on the run strip.

The crew sees the aircraft's real state where it checks an engine, the gear or a pressure, not the indication a failed instrument would give. It counts an engine as running once its N2 passes 50 %, short of a settled idle.
The crew's pace is fixed: about 1.5 s between items, with each item's own timing for switches and tests. It is not tied to the checklist's length or the phase of flight.
The crew assumes you are in the left seat as pilot flying throughout; there is no handover of pilot flying to the first officer.
Some items that a real crew member would set or test are answered with nothing moved: see [Items the crew answers without setting them](#answered-items).

The checklists are the EFB's versions of the books, with some items left out and some added (the DC-10's STARTING ENGINES, BEFORE TAXI, PASSING 10,000 FT and LEAVING AIRCRAFT, the KC-10's STARTING ENGINES and PASSING 10,000 FT, the MD-10's STARTING ENGINES and PASSING 10,000 FT), so that each thing the crew does has an item.
Ticks and the crew's modes are kept with the aircraft across sessions; a run in progress is not. After a reload or a variant change, start the checklist again.

At BEFORE START the S/O cannot set their oxygen regulator and stops the run on the Oxygen item (“OXY SUPPLY LEVER is not wired yet”). Tick it to go on. The S/O does not work the flight deck access system: the FDAS items are answered with nothing moved.

The pneumatic configuration the S/O sets after start and after takeoff has every supply and pack on. Operators often fly with fewer packs; set the panel yourself after the item if you prefer, and the S/O will leave it until the next item that sets it.
The S/O does not end the tank 2 transfer they open at BEFORE TAKEOFF with more than 40,000 lb in tank 2, unless a cruise CG target is set and they take the fuel panel over in the cruise.
Only the main tanks take part in the cruise CG management; auxiliary tanks are not managed by the crew.
The air tankers' drop system and the Omega's air refueling pods have no crew items. On those aircraft the Virtual Crew works the DC-10 card only.
The boom operator's checklist items are answered by the FE. The boom operator's own station and the air refueling procedures have no crew items, and the body tanks are not managed by the crew.
The tanker's seat belt switch is never moved by the crew.
The MD-10 has no autobrake selector in this cockpit, so every autobrake item is answered as not installed.

With a systems panel in MANUAL the F/O works only some of the book's [MANUAL] steps: the hydraulic checks and RMPs, and the tank pumps before start and at parking. The fuel panel check and the after-takeoff transfers are yours.

blocks.content: Failures injected from the EFB's [Failures app](efb#failures-app) reach the crew as they reach you: an APU generator failure brings the ground request on the DC-10 and KC-10 and stops the MD-10's APU Start item; a hydraulic failure stops the KC-10 and MD-10 items that check the system, and a generator failure the KC-10's before-takeoff electrical check, while the DC-10's checks wait a set time and carry on. They are a good way to practice the crew's behavior on the ground.

parts.title: Ground Operations and Towing
parts.summary: Ground power and air, servicing, chocks and covers, pushback and towing.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: How the simulation provides the ramp: who brings each service, what it does to the aircraft, and when it may be called.

blocks.content: On the line, everything that happens to the aircraft between block-in and pushback is done by people outside it: the ramp agent who chocks the wheels and plugs in the ground power, the air-start and air-conditioning carts, the fueller, the caterers, the lavatory truck, the loaders, the de-icing crew and the tug driver. The flight crew ask for each service, check that it has been done, and work the aircraft's own side of it: EXT PWR on, the pneumatic supply selected for a start, the doors armed, the parking brake set or released at the ground crew's call.

In the simulation the crew ask through the EFB's **Ground Ops** app, and the ground equipment is simulated as equipment: a cart drives up, is connected and delivers what a real cart delivers into the aircraft's own systems; a set of chocks holds the wheels; a tug is a vehicle of its own, coupled to the nose gear by a towbar with a shear pin. Each piece of equipment is drawn at the aircraft while it is there, with hoses, cables and streamers, and the carts and trucks make their own sounds while they work. The ramp equipment is drawn only for your aircraft, not for AI or multiplayer DC-10s.

Each service has one provider at a time. Without GSX Pro, the EFB provides everything. With GSX Pro running and chosen in Settings, GSX's vehicles provide the services GSX has, and the EFB keeps those GSX does not: the air-start and conditioned-air carts, the chocks and covers, and its own tow tug. The simulator's own pushback tug can be used too.
