Generator control relay: energizes the generator's field. See [Electrical](electrical).
Generator control unit: regulates a generator's voltage, controls its relays and protects its channel. See [Electrical](electrical).
General Electric; on speed cards, gear extend.
The bar that holds the escape slide's apron; arming the slide locks it to the floor so the slide deploys as the door opens. See [Doors and Cabin](doors-and-cabin).
Galley load control unit: the contactor that feeds a galley bus.
The discontinued approach and climb away; flown with go-around thrust and the TO/GA or G/A mode.
Ground power unit: the external power cart.
Ground proximity warning system: warns of dangerous closure with terrain, descent after takeoff, an unsafe configuration, glideslope deviation and windshear. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
Generator relay: connects a generator to its generator bus; also gear retract (speed), and gross (GR WT).
The float-operated valve that lets outboard compartment fuel run into the main compartment of a wing tank.
The shortest path between two points on the earth's surface, the route an inertial or FMS system flies.
The lower idle speed used on the ground.
The ground and flight signals from the landing gear that switch systems between their ground and flight logic (the FedEx and KC-10 "ground shift"). See [Landing Gear](landing-gear).
Glideslope; ground speed; on the MD-10 electrical synoptic, ground service bus.
Ground service relay: connects external power to the AC ground service bus.
FSDreamTeam's ground services add-on for MSFS, which the EFB can call.
Galley transfer relay: switches a galley bus between its generator bus and galley external power.
How an inertial platform finds true north during alignment, by sensing the earth's rotation. See [Navigation](navigation).
(KC-10) GPS integrity figures on the GPS SENSOR page: horizontal alert limit, horizontal protection level, horizontal figure of merit and horizontal uncertainty level.
(KC-10) The USAF 463L master pallet, 88 × 108 in, the only pallet the KC-10's cargo floor takes.
Heading (HDG SEL, HDG HOLD; HDG/TRK on the MD-10).
High frequency: the long-range radios, whose sky wave carries far beyond line of sight. See [Communications](communications).
The higher-pressure compressor bleed port, used when the low stage cannot supply enough pressure, at low engine power. See [Pneumatics](pneumatics).
The time a de-icing or anti-icing fluid is expected to protect the aircraft from further ice in falling precipitation. See [Adverse Weather](adverse-weather).
An engine start in which EGT rises fast or exceeds the start limit. See [Engines](engines).
(MD-10) Hydraulic system controller: manages the pumps and motor pumps automatically. See [Hydraulics](hydraulics).
Horizontal situation indicator: the compass card with course and glideslope deviation. See [Flight Instruments](flight-instruments).
Honeywell/Trimble GPS navigation management system (DC-10 fit), three units with MCDUs. See [Flight Management](flight-management).
An engine start that lights but stops accelerating short of idle. See [Engines](engines).
(AINS-70) Inertial: the navigation mode using the inertial sensor systems alone.
Indicated airspeed: the airspeed the instruments show, from impact pressure.
Identification: a station's identifier, a database ident, or the transponder's ident pulse.
(KC-10) Independent disconnect system: a boom disconnect path with its own pressure source (the INDEP DISC gauge), usable when the normal disconnect is not. See [Air Refueling](air-refueling).
(KC-10) Identification friend or foe: the military transponder (AN/APX-119), operated through the FMS. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
Inlet guide vanes: the variable vanes ahead of the first compressor stage.
Instrument landing system: localizer and glideslope beams, with marker beacons. See [Navigation](navigation).
Intermix: the thrust rating computer position that sets a separate limit for intermixed engine types (not used on any simulated aircraft).
Total pressure less static pressure: the dynamic pressure the airspeed indicator measures. See [Flight Instruments](flight-instruments).
(KC-10) The FMS navigation pages (INAV SELECT) on which the designated navigation solution is chosen.
Independent (INDEP DISC, the boom's independent disconnect).
The bending relief that the weight of the engines and wing fuel gives the wing root in flight; the reason the wing tanks are emptied last. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
Collins inertial navigation system (DC-10 fit). See [Navigation](navigation).
(KC-10) Inertial navigation unit: three Litton LTN-101 units controlled from the FMS. See [Navigation](navigation).
(AINS-70) Initial program load: reloading a computer's program and database from tape.
(MD-10) Inertial reference system: the inertial part of the ADIRUs, aligned from the MCDU.
International standard atmosphere: 15 °C and 1013.25 hPa at sea level, falling about 2 °C per 1,000 ft.
(AINS-70) Inertial sensor display unit: reads and initializes the platforms.
A valve in the pneumatic manifold that separates or joins the bleed sources (1-3, 1-2 and the APU/ISOL valve). See [Pneumatics](pneumatics).
(AINS-70) Inertial sensor system: one of the three inertial platforms.
Jet A, Jet A-1, Jet B
Civil jet fuels: Jet A and A-1 kerosene, Jet B wide-cut.
A pump with no moving parts that uses a fast stream of fluid or air to entrain and move a larger flow (fuel transfer and scavenge, cargo heating).
Military jet fuels: JP-4 wide-cut (like Jet B), JP-5 high flash point, JP-8 kerosene (like Jet A-1). See [Limitations](limitations).
Pratt & Whitney high-bypass turbofan; the JT9D-59A powers the DC-10-40 and sets thrust by EPR. See [Engines](engines).
The McDonnell Douglas KC-10A Extender, the USAF tanker and cargo derivative of the DC-10-30; in this manual also the aircraft button. See [Aircraft General](aircraft-general).
The Dutch air force tanker conversion of the DC-10-30; simulated as a plain DC-10-30.
(PMS) Drag and fuel flow factors that tune the predictions to an individual airframe.
The original electromechanical ADI and HSI fit offered on the DC-10.
Knot: one nautical mile per hour.
Latitude; on the trim handles, lateral.
Industry designations of unit load devices (containers and pallets) carried in the lower holds.
Left emergency control relay: closed by selecting emergency power, it connects the battery direct bus to the left emergency DC bus and the static inverter to the left emergency AC bus.
Leading edge of the mean aerodynamic chord, the reference for %MAC.
(MD-10) Left and right emergency buses, as labeled on the electrical synoptic.

(MD-10) Alert levels on the EAD: 3 red and boxed (emergency, MASTER WARNING), 2 amber and boxed (abnormal, MASTER CAUTION), 1 amber (maintenance or configuration), 0 cyan (status). See [Warning Systems](warning-systems).
Lower main circuit breaker panel, as a breaker location (LM A-15).
Lift divided by weight, in g; 1.0 in level flight and the reciprocal of the cosine of the bank angle in a level turn. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
The division of the AC load equally between paralleled generators, by trimming each drive's speed (real load) and each generator's excitation (reactive load). See [Electrical](electrical).
The anti-skid function that dumps a wheel's brake pressure when it turns slower than 11 mph while its partner across the aircraft turns faster than 29 mph. See [Landing Gear](landing-gear).
Longitude; on the trim handles, longitudinal.
The lower-pressure compressor bleed port, used in climb and cruise. See [Pneumatics](pneumatics).
Line replaceable unit: a box that is changed as a whole.
Lower and upper sideband (HF modes; USB is the aeronautical standard).
Line select key (beside each line of an MCDU or CDU screen).
Linear variable differential transformer: a position transducer.
Left wing down, right wing down (aileron trim).
Mean aerodynamic chord: the chord of an equivalent rectangular wing, the reference for CG position. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
True airspeed divided by the local speed of sound.
The nose-down pitching tendency at high Mach as the center of lift moves aft (transonic tuck). See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
Missed approach point; also the ND's map mode.
The amber and red glareshield lights that draw the crew to any caution or warning; pushing one cancels it and re-arms it for the next fault. See [Warning Systems](warning-systems).
(DC-10 air tanker) The computer that runs a retardant drop through the three tank controllers. See [Aerial Firefighting](aerial-firefighting).
(KC-10) Maximum allowable weight when V1 = VMCG: the weight at which a stop from VMCG still fits the runway.
Maximum, minimum (also autobrake settings, with MED).
Multipurpose control display unit: the FMS keyboard and screen (MD-10; DC-10 with the HT-9100). See [Flight Management](flight-management).
(DC-10, KC-10) Maximum cruise thrust: the thrust rating computer's CR limit.
The FedEx conversion of the DC-10 to a two-crew glass flight deck derived from the MD-11, in -10 and -30 versions; in this manual also the aircraft button. See [Aircraft General](aircraft-general).
The DC-10's successor, from which the MD-10's flight deck is derived.
Main engine control: the CF6's hydromechanical fuel control. See [Engines](engines).
Mechanic (the button that sounds the horn in the nose wheel well to call the ground crew).
Multifunction display: the electronic ADI and HSI attitude display fit offered on the DC-10.
(KC-10) The FMS navigation solutions blending INU 1 or INU 2 with the military GPS receiver (GPS3).
The lowest speed at which the aircraft can be kept straight after a wing engine failure: VMCG on the ground, VMCA in the air. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
The speed at which total drag is least; below it the aircraft is speed-unstable. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
The speed giving enough margin above the stall to maneuver in a configuration: 1.5 VS clean and slats only, 1.4 VS at 22/EXT. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
Miscellaneous (on the MD-10, a cue switch and alert group).
Modified: an FMS page with changes awaiting EXEC.
(KC-10) Mission (the FMS key that builds the refueling patterns).
Mode selector unit: the overhead switch that selects an inertial system's mode, from off through align to navigate and attitude (AINS-70, Carousel IV-A, INS-61B).
Low-pressure (fan) rotor speed in percent; the thrust-setting parameter of the CF6. See [Engines](engines).
(CF6) The rise of 1 to 2 % N1 through the takeoff roll as the engine's temperatures settle, with no throttle movement.
High-pressure (core) rotor speed in percent. See [Engines](engines).
(MD-10) No-break power transfer: the electrical system brings an incoming source into phase and parallels it briefly, so the bus is not interrupted. See [Electrical](electrical).
(AINS-70) Navigation computer unit: one of two computers that blend all sensors into one position.
Navigation display (MD-10; DC-10 with the FPDS fit).
The point at which the extra lift of an angle-of-attack change acts; with the CG ahead of it the aircraft is statically stable. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
(HT-9100) Navigation processor unit: holds the GPS receiver, database and flight management functions.
Non-reversible motor pump: a hydraulic motor driven by one system that drives a pump for another, in one direction only (the 2-1 and 3-2 pumps). See [Hydraulics](hydraulics).
The fuel a tanker gives, and the fuel a receiver takes, in air refueling.
Operational flight plan (as imported from SimBrief).
Overhead circuit breaker panel, as a breaker location (OH A-13).
The altitude giving the best fuel mileage for the weight; it rises as fuel burns off. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
The valve that controls cabin pressure by metering air overboard. See [Air Conditioning](air-conditioning).
Passenger address; in performance fields, pressure altitude.
An air conditioning unit that cools and dries bleed air with heat exchangers and an air cycle machine. See [Air Conditioning](air-conditioning).

(DC-10) Performance and failure assessment monitor: the autoland option that shows each pilot a predicted touchdown point and calls TAKEOVER if the landing looks unsafe. See [Automatic Flight](automatic-flight).
The canopy and ring at the end of a refueling hose that forms the receiver's target and couples the probe. See [Air Refueling Systems](air-refueling-systems).
Running the generators connected together on the AC tie bus, in phase and sharing load. See [Electrical](electrical).
Preconditioned air: the ground cart that heats or cools the cabin without the packs.
Power control unit: the tandem hydraulic actuator that moves a primary flight control surface, each piston fed by a different system. See [Flight Controls](flight-controls).
Primary flight display (MD-10; DC-10 with the FPDS fit).
The fire retardant the DC-10 air tanker carries in the simulation (Phos-Chek LC-95A-Fx, 9.01 lb/gal).
The slow pitch oscillation, a minute or more long, in which the aircraft trades speed for height and back at nearly constant angle of attack. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
(Carousel IV-A) Desired performance index: the accuracy level chosen for radio updating.
A duct pierced with many small holes that spreads hot bleed air evenly along the inside of a slat. See [Ice and Rain](ice-and-rain).

Pitch limit indicator: feathered bars on the attitude display, set above the aircraft symbol by the pitch the aircraft can gain before stick shaker angle of attack. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
A door larger than its opening, held shut by cabin pressure. See [Doors and Cabin](doors-and-cabin).
Permanent magnet generator: the small generator inside each main generator that supplies the GCU and the exciter field. See [Electrical](electrical).
Performance management system: the DC-10-30 and -40 option that computes economy speeds, thrust targets and a vertical profile to the bottom of descent. See [Flight Management](flight-management).
Pilot not flying: the older term for the pilot monitoring, used in some checklists and Virtual Crew callouts.
Predictive RAIM: a forecast of GPS integrity at the destination or approach time.
The movement of a gyro's spin axis at right angles to an applied torque; the basis of gyro erection and also of gyro drift. See [Flight Instruments](flight-instruments).
The stabilized position behind and below the tanker from which the receiver moves in to contact. See [Air Refueling](air-refueling).
The heat exchanger in each engine pylon that cools bleed air with fan air. See [Pneumatics](pneumatics).
(DC-10, KC-10) The logic that picks the generator feeding the AC tie bus in the order 2, 1, 3 when the generators are not paralleled. See [Electrical](electrical).
A TCAS resolution advisory that asks only that the vertical speed not be changed into a forbidden range. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
(MD-10) Profile: the FMS vertical guidance mode. See [Automatic Flight](automatic-flight).
Static pressure at the compressor discharge.
Total pressure at the engine inlet.
Total pressure at the low-pressure turbine discharge; Pt7/Pt2 is the EPR.
The position computed from the inertial platform alone, kept separate from the radio-updated position.
The altimeter setting at which the altimeter reads zero on the airfield.
The altimeter setting at which the altimeter reads the airfield's elevation on the ground.
(AINS-70) Radio: the navigation mode using VOR/DME or two DMEs with no platform in NAV.
An area with no returns, not even ground returns, behind an intense weather echo, where the beam could not penetrate. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
Receiver autonomous integrity monitoring: the GPS receiver's check of its own solution.
Range divided by closure rate: the TCAS estimate of the time to closest approach. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
Ram air turbine: drives the fuel pump of each wing air refueling pod, whose pressure in turn drives the hose reel. See [Air Refueling Systems](air-refueling-systems).
Remote control circuit breaker: a breaker-relay for a large feeder.
Runway condition reading: a braking friction figure, 23 for dry downward. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
Right emergency isolation relay: separates DC bus 3 and the DC cabin bus from the right emergency DC bus when that bus is on emergency power.
Response (the KC-10 hose reel's RESP INOP light and REEL RESP RESET).
Retard: the autothrottle mode that closes the throttles in the flare (RETD in the ATS window).
Right emergency transfer relay: transfers the right emergency AC bus from generator bus 3 to the ADG.
A hydraulic motor-pump pair linking two systems that can drive in either direction, passing power without exchanging fluid (the 1-3 and 2-3 pumps; MD-10 RMP). See [Hydraulics](hydraulics).
(AINS-70) Radio/inertial: the normal navigation mode, inertial updated by VOR/DME or DME.
The property of a spinning gyro to hold its axis fixed in space when no torque acts on it. See [Flight Instruments](flight-instruments).
Radio magnetic indicator: a compass card with needles pointing to VOR or ADF stations.
(MD-10) Reversible motor pump (HYD 1-3 RMP, HYD 2-3 RMP).
Required navigation performance: the position accuracy a route or approach demands, compared with the ANP. See [Flight Management](flight-management).
The autoland mode after main gear touchdown, which steers on the localizer and lowers the nose.
The fast, non-oscillating decay of a roll rate after the ailerons are centerd. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
(KC-10) Roll-out range: the planned distance between tanker and receiver as the tanker rolls out of the rendezvous turn, in LEAD or TRAIL mode.
A compressor stall confined to cells of separated flow that travel around the annulus, with reduced airflow and rising EGT. See [Engines](engines).
Report (ALT RPT and ALT RPTS, altitude reporting).
Runway surface condition: depth of standing water or slush. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
Required time of arrival (an FMS function).
Water driven aft of a heated area that refreezes behind it. See [Ice and Rain](ice-and-rain).
Static air temperature: the temperature of the undisturbed air, derived from TAT and Mach.
Satellite communications (not fitted in the simulation).
Pumping out the last fuel or oil from a tank or sump into the main flow (fuel scavenge, oil scavenge pumps).

The design of an inertial platform's leveling loop to the 84.4-minute Schuler period, so that accelerations do not tilt it and errors oscillate rather than grow. See [Navigation](navigation#schuler-tuning).
(MD-10) System display: display unit 4, carrying the synoptic, status and consequences pages. See [Warning Systems](warning-systems).
(MD-10) System display control panel, with the cue switches.
The engine-out climb at V2 with the gear up and takeoff flaps, from gear-up to the acceleration height. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
Selective calling: a ground station's coded tone that sounds a chime in the cockpit.
Sensing (the L and R GND SENS circuit breakers).
The quick, heavily damped pitch oscillation at nearly constant speed. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
Flight with the airflow striking the aircraft from one side of the nose.
Signal (air refueling signal system, BREAKAWAY SIG).
The online flight planning service whose OFP the EFB and FMS can import. See [EFB](efb).
The subsection at the end of each part that says what the simulation models, simplifies or leaves out.
(MD-10) Source input select panel: each pilot's panel for selecting alternate air data (CADC), inertial (IRS), VOR and approach sources and the EIS source.
The region between the end of an HF ground wave and the first return of the sky wave, where nothing is heard. See [Communications](communications).
An HF signal refracted back to earth by the ionosphere, hundreds or thousands of miles from the transmitter. See [Communications](communications).
The straight-line distance from the aircraft to a DME station, which includes the height.
Single (SNGL LAND on the DC-10, SINGLE LAND on the MD-10: the fail-passive autoland).
Second officer: FedEx's title for the DC-10 flight engineer.
Speed (autothrottle speed mode, speed windows and knobs).
The tendency of the aircraft to return to its trimmed speed at constant thrust; absent below the minimum drag speed. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
The slow tendency after a bank disturbance either to roll back level (stable) or to tighten into a descending turn (unstable). See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
Slat retract (speed); (AINS-70) single radio navigation mode.
(AINS-70) Single radio/inertial: as R/I but with radio data insufficient for full RNAV accuracy.
The unit that turns battery DC into 115 V, 400 Hz single-phase AC for the left emergency AC bus on emergency power. See [Electrical](electrical).

The distance from the center of gravity forward of the neutral point, as a fraction of the mean aerodynamic chord: the measure of static stability. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
Sensitivity time control: the weather radar's reduction of gain at short range so echoes of equal strength paint the same at any distance.
A climb to the next cruise level as weight falls, to stay near the optimum altitude.
The column vibrator that warns of an approaching stall. See [Flight Controls](flight-controls).
(DC-10, KC-10) One of the five red lights on the pilots' annunciator panel (EMER BUS OFF, PNEU MANFLD FAIL, CABIN ALT, PNEU TEMP HI, APU FIRE) that repeat warnings from the flight engineer's panel.
A breakdown of the whole compressor's pressure rise: the air briefly flows backwards with a loud bang, N1 and N2 drop and EGT jumps. See [Engines](engines).
Satellite vehicle (SV USED, the number of GPS satellites in the solution).
(MD-10) A system display page showing a system's schematic with its alerts and consequences. See [Warning Systems](warning-systems).
(CF6) The low-pressure turbine inlet station, where EGT is measured.
Tactical air navigation: the military UHF navigation aid giving bearing and distance, also used air to air for rendezvous. See [Navigation](navigation).
(DC-10) The PAFAM's command to the crew to take over manually when it predicts an unsafe automatic landing.
True airspeed: the speed through the air mass.
Total air temperature: the temperature of the air brought to rest in the probe, warmer than SAT by the ram rise. See [Flight Instruments](flight-instruments).
Traffic alert and collision avoidance system: interrogates nearby transponders and gives traffic and resolution advisories. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
Time compliance technical order (a USAF modification instruction).
The minimum terrain clearance that GPWS mode 4C protects after takeoff, growing with the climb. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
The speed over the threshold at 50 ft in the landing configuration: VREF on the civil aircraft, VTH on the KC-10. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
Track angle error: the angle between the actual and the desired track.
Tape low: the DAR's signal that three quarters of its tape is used.
Telescope (the KC-10 boom's extendable inner tube).
Takeoff (as in T.O. FLX on the thrust rating computer); also Technical Order, the USAF manual series (T.O. 1C-10(K)A-1 is the KC-10 flight manual).
A gentle tanker descent during refueling that lets a power-limited receiver keep up and stay in contact. See [Air Refueling](air-refueling).
(KC-10) Takeoff and landing data, worked on the TOLD card. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
The anti-skid function that holds the aft main wheel brakes released in the air, so the aircraft cannot land on locked wheels; braking starts as the wheels spin up.
Turn point (synthesized by a direct-to on the HT-9100).
Transformer-rectifier: one of four units (TR 1, 2A, 2B, 3) that convert AC into 28 V DC. See [Electrical](electrical).
The rear part of the fan nacelle that moves aft to deploy the thrust reverser. See [Engines](engines).
(DC-10, KC-10) Thrust rating computer: computes the N1 (EPR) limit for the selected mode (takeoff, go-around, climb, maximum continuous, cruise). See [Engines](engines).
Hot bleed air added downstream of the packs to set each zone's temperature. See [Air Conditioning](air-conditioning).
(Carousel IV-A) The blending of the positions of all three inertial units.
Track (on FMA modes such as LOC TRK and G/S TRK, the beam being tracked).
The Garrett auxiliary power unit fitted to every variant. See [APU](apu).
Total temperature at the low-pressure turbine discharge (the JT9D's EGT station).
Turbulence (the autopilot's TURB mode); turbine (TURB INLET TEMP).
TCAS vertical speed indicator: a VSI with traffic and resolution advisory display.
The tires' placard ground speed (204 kt on the -30 and KC-10), which can cap the takeoff weight on a hot, high day. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).

(KC-10) Universal air refueling receptacle slipway installation: the receptacle on top of the fuselage through which the KC-10A takes fuel from a boom tanker. See [Air Refueling Systems](air-refueling-systems).
Upper and lower sideband data (HF modes).
Ultra high frequency: the military line-of-sight communications band (KC-10). See [Communications](communications).
Unit load device: a container or pallet.
The air space above the liquid in a tank.
Upper main circuit breaker panel, as a breaker location (UM B-17).
The clean flap/slat handle position: flaps up, slats retracted.
Upper and lower sideband voice (HF modes).
Decision speed: an engine failure recognized before V1, stop; at or after V1, continue. Not below VMCG, not above VR or VMBE. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
Takeoff safety speed: the engine-out climb-out speed.
(MD-10) The slat retraction speed as the FMS shows it (VSR/V3); the engine-out profile accelerates to it at the EO ACCEL altitude.
Design maneuvering speed: below it, full control deflections will not overstress the structure.
Approach speed: the threshold speed plus the wind additive.
(HT-9100) Vertical bearing: the flight path angle from present position to a chosen point.
Variable bypass valve: (CF6) a valve that spills booster air into the fan stream at low speed. See [Engines](engines).
(KC-10) Critical engine failure speed: the speed at which an engine failure leaves the same distance to stop as to go.
Design dive speed and Mach number.
The speed at which the critical engine is assumed to fail.
Visual flight rules; also the flap retraction speed (with VSR, the slat retraction speed).
Very high frequency: the line-of-sight band of the communication radios and of the VOR and ILS receivers.
(MD-10) Versatile integrated avionics: the three computers that draw the display units and host the FMS.
The simulation's crew automation, which runs flows and checklists for the other crew members. See [Virtual Crew](virtual-crew).
(DC-10) VOR/LOC: the autopilot mode selector position for a VOR course or a localizer alone.
Very large air tanker: the firefighting class of the DC-10 air tanker. See [Aerial Firefighting](aerial-firefighting).
Maximum speed with the landing gear extended.
Maximum speed for operating the landing gear (VLO RET, VLO EXT).
Maximum speed (VMO/MMO or the flap placard), the ceiling of speed envelope protection.
Maximum brake energy speed: the highest speed from which a stop stays within the brakes' energy capacity.
Minimum control speed in the air: control with full rudder and no more than 5° of bank after a wing engine failure.
Minimum control speed on the ground: control with rudder alone after a wing engine failure, within 25 ft of the centerline.
Minimum speed (1.3 VS of the configuration, bank-compensated), the floor of speed envelope protection.
The maximum operating speed and Mach number: VMO below the crossover altitude, MMO above it. See [Limitations](limitations).
A co-located VOR and TACAN station.
Reference (threshold) speed: 1.3 times the stall speed in the landing configuration, 1.35 with the slats retracted.
(KC-10) Minimum rotation speed: the wet or icy VMCG.
V-speeds (the MD-10 FMS message CHECK/CONFIRM VSPDS).
(MD-10) Windshear alert and guidance system, part of the AFS. See [Automatic Flight](automatic-flight).
Wing air refueling pod: a self-contained hose-and-drogue unit under each wing (KC-10; DC-10-40 Omega). See [Air Refueling Systems](air-refueling-systems).
The tendency of the aircraft on the ground to turn its nose into a crosswind. See [Flight Characteristics](flight-characteristics).
The ratio of fuel flow to compressor discharge pressure, the quantity the main engine control schedules for acceleration and deceleration. See [Engines](engines).
World Geodetic System 1984, the standard navigation datum.

The increment added to the threshold speed for wind: half the steady wind above 20 kt or the full gust, whichever is greater, at least 5 kt and not more than 20 kt. See [Mission Planning](mission-planning).
An in-flight restart using the airflow turning the engine, without the starter; needs at least 10 % N2. See [Engines](engines).
(MD-10) Weather/turbulence: a weather radar mode; its turbulence detection is not modeled.
Cross-tie: the DC X-TIE switch, which with DC TIE 1 and 3 joins or splits the DC buses.
Cross-track error: the perpendicular distance from the desired track.
The system that moves the rudder automatically to damp Dutch roll and coordinate turns. See [Automatic Flight](automatic-flight).
Zero fuel weight: the weight of the aircraft with everything but usable fuel.
Center of gravity at zero fuel weight.
The weather radar relation between reflectivity (Z) and rainfall rate (R) on which the color levels are calibrated. See [Surveillance](surveillance).
